reason: The text depicts the Hebrew people (through their leaders Moses and Aaron) actively expressing their views and demands to Pharaoh. God repeatedly commands Moses to approach Pharaoh and speak (בֹּא אֶל־ פַּרְעֹה), and Moses is shown negotiating multiple times regarding the release of the people and the terms for worship in the wilderness. The Israelites are given explicit instructions to prepare and observe the Passover, demonstrating clear communication and expression of their religious practices. While Pharaoh eventually tells Moses not to appear before him again, this occurs after numerous expressions have already taken place and represents a specific rebuff rather than a systemic discouragement of the Hebrew people. The overall narrative shows active dialogue, negotiation, and expression of views by the Hebrew leadership.
